commit_message:
[Build][AMDGPU] Use bitcode from the official ROCM distribution (#25133)

With the sunset of the old artifacts from
`shark-infra/amdgpu-device-libs`, migrate to LLVM bitcode blobs from the
official distribution. The version shall be pinned in
`build_tools/third_party/amdgpu_device_libs/rocm_package.json`.

This increases the bitcode download to 146Mb (in comparison, the WASI
SDK weighs in at <120Mb). Considering we're only using less than 1Mb,
that's unfortunate, but at the moment it's the only way to use the
official maintained source.

Fixes #25131.

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert integral float zero points of PT2E ops

PT2E accepts float zero points, and exports of asymmetric weights can
store integer zero points as floats. The conversion only accepted float
zero points that are all zero, so such ops were left for the
Torch-to-Linalg lowering, which handles no float zero points either. A
constant float zero point whose values are integers within the bounds
now converts exactly to an i32 constant. Fractional and non-constant
float zero points are still left for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering.

Part of #24862.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>

PT2E accepts float zero points, and exports of asymmetric weights can
store integer zero points as floats. The conversion only accepted float

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@1bd41d70d179 (#25129)

The upstream LLVM bazel build broke, hence I cherry-picked this fix
commit:
-
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/aa5c7b777908364447188c64fbf737141af496d1

Moreover, I had to make some changes to IREE itself:

1) Store a global `LibraryOptionsContext`
- needed because `PassBuilder` now takes a `LLVMContext&` with those
options
- `PipelineTuningOptions` combines settings supplied by IREE with those
provided by the context
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/233150

2) Remove workaround for AMDGPU loop unrolling
- no longer needed as of
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/223291
 - this used to be handled in `ROCMTarget.cpp` by overriding an option

3) Adapt to target-specific passes being split out of MLIRGpuTransforms
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/234903
- AMD-specific `populateGpu...Patterns` now live in
MLIRGPUROCDLTransforms
   - header is `mlir/Dialect/GPU/Transforms/ROCDL/Passes.h`
- still need to link `iree_compiler_API_SharedImpl` against the
now-split target libs, because MLIRCAPIGPU references them

4) Update lit tests related to softmax, which now uses a finite
reduction identity
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/232257

5) Adjust LLVMGPULegalizeNDVectors to work with new `tensor.extract`
folding
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/228686
 - added two lit cases in `legalize_nd_vectors.mlir`

6) Remove workaround for packed reductions
- fixed in upstream by: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/221430
 - keeping it would remap index twice, which would be incorrect

Assisted-by: Codex

Signed-off-by: Maksymilian B. Knust <knust@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@1bd41d70d179 (#25129)

The upstream LLVM bazel build broke, hence I cherry-picked this fix
commit:
-
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/aa5c7b777908364447188c64fbf737141af496d1

Moreover, I had to make some changes to IREE itself:

1) Store a global `LibraryOptionsContext`
- needed because `PassBuilder` now takes a `LLVMContext&` with those
options
- `PipelineTuningOptions` combines settings supplied by IREE with those
provided by the context
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/233150

2) Remove workaround for AMDGPU loop unrolling
- no longer needed as of
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/223291
 - this used to be handled in `ROCMTarget.cpp` by overriding an option

3) Adapt to target-specific passes being split out of MLIRGpuTransforms
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/234903
- AMD-specific `populateGpu...Patterns` now live in
MLIRGPUROCDLTransforms
   - header is `mlir/Dialect/GPU/Transforms/ROCDL/Passes.h`
- still need to link `iree_compiler_API_SharedImpl` against the
now-split target libs, because MLIRCAPIGPU references them

4) Update lit tests related to softmax, which now uses a finite
reduction identity
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/232257

5) Adjust LLVMGPULegalizeNDVectors to work with new `tensor.extract`
folding
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/228686
 - added two lit cases in `legalize_nd_vectors.mlir`

6) Remove workaround for packed reductions
- fixed in upstream by: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/221430
 - keeping it would remap index twice, which would be incorrect

Assisted-by: Codex

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert integral float zero points of PT2E ops

PT2E accepts float zero points, and exports of asymmetric weights can
store integer zero points as floats. The conversion only accepted float
zero points that are all zero, so such ops were left for the
Torch-to-Linalg lowering, which handles no float zero points either. A
constant float zero point whose values are integers within the bounds
now converts exactly to an i32 constant. Fractional and non-constant
float zero points are still left for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering.

Part of #24862.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: pr-greeter

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert integral float zero points of PT2E ops

PT2E accepts float zero points, and exports of asymmetric weights can
store integer zero points as floats. The conversion only accepted float
zero points that are all zero, so such ops were left for the
Torch-to-Linalg lowering, which handles no float zero points either. A
constant float zero point whose values are integers within the bounds
now converts exactly to an i32 constant. Fractional and non-constant
float zero points are still left for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering.

commit_message:
[Stream] Make "consolidate" mode of SplitParameterEncoding actually consolidate (#25040)

Fixes iree-org/iree#24920. By design, the `includeUnmodified=true`
("consolidate") setting should move all parameters out of the main
module, including the ones that are still bound to be encoded online.
However, the pass design was preventing this from happening:
`includeUnmodified` wasn't looked at and "raw" weights weren't
considered when filtering out the encoding computations deemed
"hoistable" and assigning encoder module locations to those.

The new approach is:
- hoist the chosen encoding computations into a temporary block and
eliminate the dead parameters from the main module;
- in "consolidate" mode, we can now claim unmodified parameters into the
encoder module as well;
- final serialization and DCE.

The change was assisted by Codex.

---------

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Alex Denisov <denisov@roofline.ai>

[Stream] Make "consolidate" mode of SplitParameterEncoding actually consolidate (#25040)

Fixes iree-org/iree#24920. By design, the `includeUnmodified=true`
("consolidate") setting should move all parameters out of the main
module, including the ones that are still bound to be encoded online.
However, the pass design was preventing this from happening:
`includeUnmodified` wasn't looked at and "raw" weights weren't
considered when filtering out the encoding computations deemed
"hoistable" and assigning encoder module locations to those.

The new approach is:
- hoist the chosen encoding computations into a temporary block and
eliminate the dead parameters from the main module;
- in "consolidate" mode, we can now claim unmodified parameters into the
encoder module as well;
- final serialization and DCE.

The change was assisted by Codex.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Write embedded executable object data before linking

Executable objects that carry inline data got a temporary file path,
but the data was never written to it.

The linker then received an empty object file.

Serialize the object data into the temporary file, then flush and close
the file so that the linker reads its complete contents.

Report an error if the temporary file cannot be created or the data
cannot be serialized.

Add a lit test in which a dispatch calls a function that only an inline
object defines, so the embedded linker reports an undefined symbol when
the object file is empty.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Romain Paquet <rpaquet@kalrayinc.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Write embedded executable object data before linking

Executable objects that carry inline data got a temporary file path,
but the data was never written to it.

The linker then received an empty object file.

Serialize the object data into the temporary file, then flush and close
the file so that the linker reads its complete contents.

Report an error if the temporary file cannot be created or the data
cannot be serialized.

Add a lit test in which a dispatch calls a function that only an inline
object defines, so the embedded linker reports an undefined symbol when
the object file is empty.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Romain Paquet <rpaquet@kalrayinc.com>
name: Build Packages / Linux Release (x86_64)

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Write embedded executable object data before linking

Executable objects that carry inline data got a temporary file path,
but the data was never written to it.

The linker then received an empty object file.

Serialize the object data into the temporary file, then flush and close
the file so that the linker reads its complete contents.

Report an error if the temporary file cannot be created or the data
cannot be serialized.

Add a lit test in which a dispatch calls a function that only an inline
object defines, so the embedded linker reports an undefined symbol when
the object file is empty.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Romain Paquet <rpaquet@kalrayinc.com>

commit_message:
[Stream] Fix scf.while region signature conversion (#25100)

I'm working on running JAX computations inside JupyterLite using IREE,
with both compilation and execution happening in the browser.

For the CPU path, I'm testing JAX tracing/autodiff → exported StableHLO
→ IREE's LLVM CPU backend → Wasm → linking/loading and execution. While
testing control flow through this pipeline, I ran into this Stream
conversion crash. I found a few other correctness issues along the way
which I'll send separately with reduced reproducers.

`scf.while` allows its operand and result signatures to differ. Its
before-region arguments match the operands, while its after-region
arguments match the results. However, `ScfWhileOpConversion` builds a
signature mapping from the operand types and applies it to both regions.

The reduced case takes one tensor into the before-region and forwards
two tensors to the after-region. Reusing the first region's mapping
crashes in `applySignatureConversion`. Although I found this during the
Wasm experiments, the same reproducer also crashes natively.

This change lets `convertRegionTypes` derive the after-region's
signature from its own arguments.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: linux_x64_gcc

commit_message:
[Stream] Fix scf.while region signature conversion (#25100)

I'm working on running JAX computations inside JupyterLite using IREE,
with both compilation and execution happening in the browser.

For the CPU path, I'm testing JAX tracing/autodiff → exported StableHLO
→ IREE's LLVM CPU backend → Wasm → linking/loading and execution. While
testing control flow through this pipeline, I ran into this Stream
conversion crash. I found a few other correctness issues along the way
which I'll send separately with reduced reproducers.

`scf.while` allows its operand and result signatures to differ. Its
before-region arguments match the operands, while its after-region
arguments match the results. However, `ScfWhileOpConversion` builds a
signature mapping from the operand types and applies it to both regions.

The reduced case takes one tensor into the before-region and forwards
two tensors to the after-region. Reusing the first region's mapping
crashes in `applySignatureConversion`. Although I found this during the
Wasm experiments, the same reproducer also crashes natively.

This change lets `convertRegionTypes` derive the after-region's
signature from its own arguments.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: runtime_tracing :: windows-2022 :: console

commit_message:
[Stream] Fix scf.while region signature conversion (#25100)

I'm working on running JAX computations inside JupyterLite using IREE,
with both compilation and execution happening in the browser.

For the CPU path, I'm testing JAX tracing/autodiff → exported StableHLO
→ IREE's LLVM CPU backend → Wasm → linking/loading and execution. While
testing control flow through this pipeline, I ran into this Stream
conversion crash. I found a few other correctness issues along the way
which I'll send separately with reduced reproducers.

`scf.while` allows its operand and result signatures to differ. Its
before-region arguments match the operands, while its after-region
arguments match the results. However, `ScfWhileOpConversion` builds a
signature mapping from the operand types and applies it to both regions.

The reduced case takes one tensor into the before-region and forwards
two tensors to the after-region. Reusing the first region's mapping
crashes in `applySignatureConversion`. Although I found this during the
Wasm experiments, the same reproducer also crashes natively.

This change lets `convertRegionTypes` derive the after-region's
signature from its own arguments.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Build][AMDGPU] Use bitcode from the official ROCM distribution (#25133)

With the sunset of the old artifacts from
`shark-infra/amdgpu-device-libs`, migrate to LLVM bitcode blobs from the
official distribution. The version shall be pinned in
`build_tools/third_party/amdgpu_device_libs/rocm_package.json`.

This increases the bitcode download to 146Mb (in comparison, the WASI
SDK weighs in at <120Mb). Considering we're only using less than 1Mb,
that's unfortunate, but at the moment it's the only way to use the
official maintained source.

Fixes #25131.

Assisted-by: Codex

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Add group_matmul and group_mmt4d ops (#24909)

# What & why

This PR introduces a new `group_matmul` operation, to be the IREE
equivalent of Torch's
[grouped_mm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.functional.grouped_mm.html).
It's purpose is to enable efficient inference of Mixture-of-Experts
models. The op is superficially similar to `linalg.matmul` and
`linalg.batch_matmul`, but cannot be expressed as a pure
`linalg.generic` without masking inactive elements, so I believe it
belongs here in LinalgExt. The description in LinalgExtOps.td gives more
info.

# How

1) We add the standard matmul encodings to LHS, RHS and result of our op
in SetEncoding.cpp
2) We define an auxillary `group_mmt4d` op - the grouped equivalent of
`mmt4d`
3) In MaterializeEncodingPatterns.cpp, we convert `group_matmul` to
`group_mmt4d`
4) We implement the tiling interface for `group_mmt4d`
5) After workgroup tiling, we add a `DecomposeGroupMmt4DPass`, which
turns `group_mmt4d` into `mmt4d` + some extra ops
a) if all input rows of a tile belong to the same expert, we just slice
+ `mmt4d`
b) otherwise, we loop over experts; for each of them we mask out rows
that don't belong to it

# Performance

Preliminary benchmarks have shown speed close to a matmul of comparable
shape. This is expected since:
- decomposition of `group_mmt4d` happens after workgroup tiling, so the
op turns into a single dispatch
 - there is no control flow on the host side
- the number of tiles containing a boundary between experts is limited:
(5a) is much more common than (5b)
- only the weights of the active experts need are accessed - no wasted
memory bandwidth

# Known shortcomings / future work
 - only LLVMCPU backend is supported currently
   - dynamic tile sizes (RVV & SVE) not implemented
 - for compilation to succeed, you must have enabled:
   - data tiling
   - distribution tiling (on by default)
 - LHS and RHS must be floats
- integer operands could result in an identity layout (not implemented)
- the attribute placed on `group_mmt4d` to support the narrow-N
transpose is an ugly hack
- this will no longer be needed once we can lower to `inner_tiled`
instead
- both ops implemented here could possibly be unified into some kind of
`group_contract`
- by analogy to
[linalg.contract](https://mlir.llvm.org/docs/Dialects/Linalg/#linalgcontract-linalgcontractop)
- instead of passing in expert offsets, perhaps LHS should just be a
proper [ragged
tensor](https://iree.dev/reference/mlir-dialects/TensorExt/#iree_tensor_extcast_to_ragged_shape-tensorextcasttoraggedshapeop)?
   - this feature is still work-in-progress IIUC
 - gather/scatter should be fused with this op

commit_message:
[Stream] Fix scf.while region signature conversion (#25100)

I'm working on running JAX computations inside JupyterLite using IREE,
with both compilation and execution happening in the browser.

For the CPU path, I'm testing JAX tracing/autodiff → exported StableHLO
→ IREE's LLVM CPU backend → Wasm → linking/loading and execution. While
testing control flow through this pipeline, I ran into this Stream
conversion crash. I found a few other correctness issues along the way
which I'll send separately with reduced reproducers.

`scf.while` allows its operand and result signatures to differ. Its
before-region arguments match the operands, while its after-region
arguments match the results. However, `ScfWhileOpConversion` builds a
signature mapping from the operand types and applies it to both regions.

The reduced case takes one tensor into the before-region and forwards
two tensors to the after-region. Reusing the first region's mapping
crashes in `applySignatureConversion`. Although I found this during the
Wasm experiments, the same reproducer also crashes natively.

This change lets `convertRegionTypes` derive the after-region's
signature from its own arguments.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Write embedded executable object data before linking

Executable objects that carry inline data got a temporary file path,
but the data was never written to it.

The linker then received an empty object file.

Serialize the object data into the temporary file, then flush and close
the file so that the linker reads its complete contents.

Report an error if the temporary file cannot be created or the data
cannot be serialized.

Add a lit test in which a dispatch calls a function that only an inline
object defines, so the embedded linker reports an undefined symbol when
the object file is empty.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

commit_message:
[Stream] Make "consolidate" mode of SplitParameterEncoding actually consolidate (#25040)

Fixes iree-org/iree#24920. By design, the `includeUnmodified=true`
("consolidate") setting should move all parameters out of the main
module, including the ones that are still bound to be encoded online.
However, the pass design was preventing this from happening:
`includeUnmodified` wasn't looked at and "raw" weights weren't
considered when filtering out the encoding computations deemed
"hoistable" and assigning encoder module locations to those.

The new approach is:
- hoist the chosen encoding computations into a temporary block and
eliminate the dead parameters from the main module;
- in "consolidate" mode, we can now claim unmodified parameters into the
encoder module as well;
- final serialization and DCE.

The change was assisted by Codex.

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@1bd41d70d179 (#25129)

The upstream LLVM bazel build broke, hence I cherry-picked this fix
commit:
-
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/aa5c7b777908364447188c64fbf737141af496d1

Moreover, I had to make some changes to IREE itself:

1) Store a global `LibraryOptionsContext`
- needed because `PassBuilder` now takes a `LLVMContext&` with those
options
- `PipelineTuningOptions` combines settings supplied by IREE with those
provided by the context
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/233150

2) Remove workaround for AMDGPU loop unrolling
- no longer needed as of
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/223291
 - this used to be handled in `ROCMTarget.cpp` by overriding an option

3) Adapt to target-specific passes being split out of MLIRGpuTransforms
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/234903
- AMD-specific `populateGpu...Patterns` now live in
MLIRGPUROCDLTransforms
   - header is `mlir/Dialect/GPU/Transforms/ROCDL/Passes.h`
- still need to link `iree_compiler_API_SharedImpl` against the
now-split target libs, because MLIRCAPIGPU references them

4) Update lit tests related to softmax, which now uses a finite
reduction identity
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/232257

5) Adjust LLVMGPULegalizeNDVectors to work with new `tensor.extract`
folding
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/228686
 - added two lit cases in `legalize_nd_vectors.mlir`

6) Remove workaround for packed reductions
- fixed in upstream by: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/221430
 - keeping it would remap index twice, which would be incorrect

Assisted-by: Codex

Signed-off-by: Maksymilian B. Knust <knust@roofline.ai>

The upstream LLVM bazel build broke, hence I cherry-picked this fix
commit:
-
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/aa5c7b777908364447188c64fbf737141af496d1

Moreover, I had to make some changes to IREE itself:

1) Store a global `LibraryOptionsContext`
- needed because `PassBuilder` now takes a `LLVMContext&` with those
options
- `PipelineTuningOptions` combines settings supplied by IREE with those
provided by the context
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/233150

2) Remove workaround for AMDGPU loop unrolling
- no longer needed as of
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/223291
 - this used to be handled in `ROCMTarget.cpp` by overriding an option

3) Adapt to target-specific passes being split out of MLIRGpuTransforms
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/234903
- AMD-specific `populateGpu...Patterns` now live in
MLIRGPUROCDLTransforms
   - header is `mlir/Dialect/GPU/Transforms/ROCDL/Passes.h`
- still need to link `iree_compiler_API_SharedImpl` against the
now-split target libs, because MLIRCAPIGPU references them

4) Update lit tests related to softmax, which now uses a finite
reduction identity
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/232257

5) Adjust LLVMGPULegalizeNDVectors to work with new `tensor.extract`
folding
 - see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/228686
 - added two lit cases in `legalize_nd_vectors.mlir`

6) Remove workaround for packed reductions
- fixed in upstream by: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/221430
 - keeping it would remap index twice, which would be incorrect

Assisted-by: Codex

Signed-off-by: Maksymilian B. Knust <knust@roofline.ai>
name: Test Android / android_arm64

reduction identity

folding

6) Remove workaround for packed reductions
- fixed in upstream by: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/221430

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert integral float zero points of PT2E ops

PT2E accepts float zero points, and exports of asymmetric weights can
store integer zero points as floats. The conversion only accepted float
zero points that are all zero, so such ops were left for the
Torch-to-Linalg lowering, which handles no float zero points either. A
constant float zero point whose values are integers within the bounds
now converts exactly to an i32 constant. Fractional and non-constant
float zero points are still left for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering.

Part of #24862.
